views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Continue negotiating firmly to close a deal on US terms — lock in the enforcement mechanism, strengthened IP protection, and China's purchase commitments, while holding the existing ~$250B tariff structure as leverage. Do not escalate in this critical week (that risks destroying a near-deal the US largely wants), but do not unilaterally roll back tariffs before binding enforcement is secured. The April 3 Washington talks have both sides reporting progress on enforcement text (event timeline) yet no final deal, so the correct posture is to hold the line and finish the deal rather than make new commitments or escalate.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is modestly negative-to-neutral because the US holds clear leverage and is near a favorable settlement, not facing an existential or high threat. The US has imposed Section 301 tariffs on ~$250B of Chinese imports (timeline: Sept 24, 2018) and China has been the more pressured party — it has agreed to increase purchases (timeline: Dec 1 G20 truce; Feb 2019 pledge on 5mT soybeans) and both presidents want a deal (US Chamber, Apr 2). This asymmetric, deal-near position reads as a mild opportunity (-0.3), tempered by real domestic costs: the farm belt is badly exposed, with soybean sales to China down ~80-94%, record 3.7B bushel stocks, and mounting 2019 planting/financial pressure (farm policy/CNN/Reuters reporting); and US macro shows a flattening yield curve (10yr 2.52 vs 2yr 2.33, ~19bp spread from ~50bp in Nov), a mild GDP-drag signal, plus consumer sentiment still strong at 97.2 (country_health). These costs argue against blithe escalation, while the favorable negotiating trajectory argues against pre-emptive concession — hence action_score 0.0 (negotiate/hold) to finalize enforcement and purchases on US terms rather than escalate (which would deepen farm and recession risk) or concede early (which would forfeit leverage).
key_factors: ~$250B US tariffs in place on Chinese imports = leverage
April 3-4 Washington talks near deal, enforcement text unresolved
Both presidents want a deal; purchase commitments (5mT soybeans) pledged
Farm belt hard-hit: soybean exports to China down ~80-94%, record 3.7B bushel stocks, acreage/loan stress
US yield curve flattening (10-2yr ~19bp) = mild GDP-drag/recession signal
Consumer sentiment strong (97.2); only modest CPI rise
Huawei/Meng extradition adds allied-friction (Canada) but not central to trade calculus
